character_arcs.name: The Hero's Journey (Positive Change Arc)
character_arcs.description: Classic transformation arc where protagonist grows from ordinary to extraordinary through trials. Based on Joseph Campbell's monomyth.

act1.ordinary_world: Character in normal life, showing flaws or limitations
act1.call_to_adventure: Event disrupts normal life, presents challenge
act1.refusal_of_call: Character hesitates due to fear or comfort
act1.meeting_mentor: Wise figure provides guidance or tools

act2.crossing_threshold: Character commits to journey, enters new world
act2.tests_allies_enemies: Faces challenges, makes friends and foes
act2.ordeal: Greatest fear faced, symbolic death and rebirth
act2.reward: Gains object, knowledge, or inner strength

act3.road_back: Returns to ordinary world with new wisdom
act3.resurrection: Final test proves transformation is real
act3.return_with_elixir: Brings benefit to community, shows growth

character_arcs.example: Luke Skywalker (Star Wars): Farm boy → refuses adventure → meets Obi-Wan → crosses to larger galaxy → faces tests → confronts fear of inadequacy → grows in Force → returns as Jedi → defeats Empire → brings hope to galaxy
character_arcs.when_to_use: Epic adventures, coming-of-age stories, fantasy, hero narratives
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Overcomes self-doubt and fear to discover inner strength and purpose
character_arcs.theme: Transformation through adversity, discovering true self

character_arcs.name: Redemption Arc (Negative to Positive)
character_arcs.description: Character starts morally flawed or villainous and transforms into better person through sacrifice and choice.

act1.established_flaws: Character clearly selfish, cruel, or morally compromised
act1.comfortable_in_darkness: Benefits from or accepts their negative traits
act1.glimpse_of_light: Small moment hints at capacity for good

act2.moral_conflict: Begins questioning their choices and worldview
act2.temptation_to_return: Old ways offer easy escape from change
act2.critical_choice: Must choose between old self and new path

act3.sacrifice: Proves change through selfless act (often at great cost)
act3.new_identity: Embraces reformed self, rejected by neither world

character_arcs.example: Ebenezer Scrooge (A Christmas Carol): Greedy miser → visited by ghosts → sees consequences of greed → faces his lonely future → chooses generosity → transforms into kind benefactor → redeems himself
character_arcs.when_to_use: Anti-hero stories, villain redemptions, moral tales, character-driven dramas
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Confronts guilt, overcomes pride, chooses empathy over self-interest
character_arcs.theme: It's never too late to change, redemption through choice and sacrifice

character_arcs.name: Fall Arc (Positive to Negative)
character_arcs.description: Character descends from morally good to corrupted, often through ambition, fear, or temptation. Tragedy arc.

act1.established_virtue: Character is good, admirable, has strong principles
act1.fatal_flaw: Subtle weakness: ambition, fear, pride, naivety
act1.initial_temptation: Opportunity to compromise values for gain

act2.first_compromise: Small moral violation, justified or rationalized
act2.slippery_slope: Each choice makes next compromise easier
act2.losing_relationships: Drives away people who could save them
act2.point_of_no_return: Major act locks them into dark path
act2.embracing_darkness: No longer rationalizes, accepts corrupted self

act3.tragic_end: Destroyed by what they became (death, isolation, or madness)

character_arcs.example: Walter White (Breaking Bad): Good teacher → cancer diagnosis → cooks meth 'for family' → enjoys power → hurts innocents → loses family → dies alone, transformed into monster
character_arcs.when_to_use: Tragedies, cautionary tales, complex villain origins, dark dramas
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Pride blinds to truth, ambition corrupts values, fear drives to cruelty
character_arcs.theme: Corruption through power, consequences of moral compromise, tragedy of wasted potential

character_arcs.name: Flat Arc (Character Changes World)
character_arcs.description: Protagonist doesn't change internally but transforms world around them through strength of conviction.

act1.world_in_lie: World around them operates on false belief

act2.influencing_others: Actions inspire others to question status quo

act3.reaffirming_truth: Doubles down on beliefs with clarity
act3.world_transforms: Others adopt the truth, system changes

character_arcs.example: Atticus Finch (To Kill a Mockingbird): Holds moral integrity → faces racist town → defends innocent man → doesn't waver despite threats → influences children and some townspeople → shifts community perspective on justice
character_arcs.when_to_use: Stories about social change, moral tales, inspirational narratives, revolutionary figures
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Maintains integrity under pressure, inspires others through example
character_arcs.theme: One person can change the world, truth prevails over comfortable lies

character_arcs.name: Disillusionment Arc (Loss of Innocence)
character_arcs.description: Character begins naive or idealistic and becomes cynical or realistic after harsh truths revealed.

act1.innocent_worldview: Character believes in goodness, fairness, simple morality

act2.harsh_truths: Repeatedly confronted with moral ambiguity, cruelty, injustice
act2.internal_conflict: Struggles to reconcile beliefs with reality

act3.new_wisdom: Gains depth, becomes more capable but less hopeful

character_arcs.example: Holden Caulfield (Catcher in the Rye): Idealistic teenager → sees adult hypocrisy → tries to protect innocence → realizes impossibility → accepts complexity of growing up → loses innocence but gains understanding
character_arcs.when_to_use: Coming-of-age stories, war narratives, loss of faith stories, dark revelations
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Innocence shattered, idealism tempered by reality, painful maturation
character_arcs.theme: Growing up means seeing darkness, loss of innocence is necessary but painful

character_arcs.name: Growth Arc (Overcoming Internal Flaw)
character_arcs.description: Character has specific internal weakness that prevents happiness, overcomes it through story events.

act1.visible_flaw: Clear character weakness: fear, selfishness, distrust, etc.
act1.wants_vs_needs: Pursues external goal but needs internal change

act2.flaw_tested: Situations expose and challenge the weakness
act2.failed_attempts: Tries to succeed without changing, fails
act2.recognition: Begins to see their flaw is the problem
act2.resistance: Fears change more than continuing pain

act3.choice_moment: Must choose between flaw and growth
act3.new_equilibrium: External goal achieved or revealed as unimportant

character_arcs.example: Mr. Darcy (Pride and Prejudice): Proud and aloof → falls for Elizabeth → his pride offends her → faces rejection → recognizes his flaw → humbles himself → overcomes pride → wins love through genuine change
character_arcs.when_to_use: Romance, character studies, personal dramas, self-discovery stories
character_arcs.psychological_journey: Acknowledges personal flaw, struggles with ego, chooses growth over comfort
character_arcs.theme: True happiness requires internal change, we are our own obstacles
